981.headline: A close look at the prizes

985.body:
"MAX-A-MILLION" offers a top prize of $1 million and thirteen prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward the smaller prizes. Games shaped like this pay out often, in small amounts. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

The second-biggest prize left on "MAX-A-MILLION" is $100,000, with five of them remaining.

The numbers for "MAX-A-MILLION" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
985.headline: Where the prize money is

988.body:
The most common win left on "Emerald 10's" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $50,000, and three of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything above about "Emerald 10's" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
988.headline: A close look at the prizes

990.body:
"LADY LUCK" is past the halfway point of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

If "LADY LUCK" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
990.headline: How far along this game is

992.body:
The top prize count on "$2 MILLION VAULT" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has one of three top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

The table below shows the full count for "$2 MILLION VAULT", with every prize level included.
992.headline: Good news: no big claims

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has had no $5,000 top prize claimed for five months. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

If you play "$5,000 Triple Play" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
993.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

994.body:
"$25,000 Triple Play" has one of four top prizes left and is past the halfway point of its run. About three-quarters of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

If you play "$25,000 Triple Play" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
994.headline: How much has sold

995.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "$200,000 Triple Play", about a quarter are still unsold. The game is past the halfway point of its run, with two of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Tomorrow's count on "$200,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
